title: Delete nodes in a rooted tree to maximize remaining max depth
description_html:
You are given an undirected tree with n nodes rooted at node 1. You may delete any number of nodes (possibly none). Deleting a node removes all its incident edges. After deletions, the remaining nodes must still contain the root 1 and the remaining graph must stay connected (i.e. still a rooted tree).

Output the maximum possible maximum depth — the maximum number of edges from the root to any remaining node — achievable after such deletions.

Input

n
n-1 lines: edges  u v

Output

One integer: the maximum achievable depth.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5. You must keep the root and maintain connectivity.

Example

5
1 2
1 3
3 4
4 5
----
3

(Longest root path 1 → 3 → 4 → 5 = 3 edges.)

See Notes — this is a reduce-to-height trap.
